notes: This record is a formal undergraduate CS concentration, not a standalone AI degree. Host bachelor award variants and declaration/recognition rules have not been independently verified.

The mapped pool follows the December 17, 2025 PDF currently linked by the undergraduate concentration directory, visually reviewed at pages 2–3. It differs from the older public concentration HTML: PDF has CS 363M Introduction to Machine Learning instead of CS 363D Data Mining, CS 371N NLP instead of CS 378 NLP, and omits the uncoded ML/AI capstone. Those HTML options are not silently combined with the PDF pool.

Nine source-listed course routes are represented. CS 343(H) and CS 363M (378H) retain the publisher’s parenthetical honors notation; they are not split into invented separately verified catalog instances. CS 378 is specifically Practical Applications of Natural Language Processing, not every course with that topics number.

Partial scope: reviewed public sources leave conflicts, exact honors/topic identities, concentration eligibility/declaration/recognition and separate grade/residence thresholds unresolved. Adviser confirmation is needed; the host degree is not certified.
The older HTML advertises 12 credit hours; individual credits are separately supported by the official Course Numbers policy, not inferred from the PDF’s four-course structure.
The source date of the PDF is not a launch date. Old 2017 CSRankings and 2018 U.S. News marketing figures on the legacy page are excluded entirely from ranking data.

Current HTML identity refresh is automated; the PDF-text parser is separately rerunnable after permitted PDF retrieval, text extraction and visual review. A successful HTML refresh does not certify PDF curriculum freshness.

Metadata pass checked all nine routes against the department directory and current general catalog. Five exact electives (CS 342, 344M, 344R, 371R, 376) now have original summaries and source-qualified prerequisites. The aggregate CS 343(H), CS 363M (378H), CS 371N and named CS 378 Practical Applications of NLP retain null descriptions/prerequisites: current public sources do not establish an exact unambiguous route match. In particular the catalog uses X-prefixed codes and Principles of Machine Learning I rather than the PDF’s printed label; no equivalence is inferred.

All nine source-printed 3xx course routes receive 3 semester credits under the separately registered official Course Numbers policy. The department’s weekly lecture hours were not used as credits. Course source_id identifies the description/prerequisite source for the five exact matches; the concentration PDF remains the requirement-pool authority, and the credit-policy source supports every numerical credit/unit value.

Bounded local policy review covered the concentration directory, dated course-list PDF, dedicated legacy page and current academic advising page. They direct current CS students to an adviser but do not establish a separate concentration grade/residence threshold, declaration deadline, recognition process or eligible host-degree list. Confirmation is needed from UT CS undergraduate advising (under-info@cs.utexas.edu), including the PDF/legacy course conflict. Broader host-degree requirements remain outside this concentration inventory; no missing numerical policy is treated as zero or no requirement.
